verdicts.quote: “Use OAuth when your app needs to access Aircall data on behalf of other users or customers.” ([developer.aircall.io](https://developer.aircall.io/docs/authentication))
verdicts.reason: Aircall exposes Basic Auth and OAuth, but for multi-tenant/public apps they direct developers to OAuth, so OAuth2 is the primary auth a toolkit would use.

verdicts.quote: “OAuth credentials — If you haven't received them yet, apply to the Tech Partner program.” ([developer.aircall.io](https://developer.aircall.io/docs/oauth))
verdicts.reason: OAuth client credentials are issued after Technology Partner approval; while API keys exist for customer admins, production OAuth for multi-tenant apps is partner-gated.

verdicts.quote: “Manage calls, messages, AI agents, users, numbers, and more — fully documented with detailed schemas, and request and response examples in the API reference.” ([developer.aircall.io](https://developer.aircall.io/docs/introduction))
verdicts.reason: The API reference covers many resource families (Users/Teams/Calls/Conversations/Campaigns/Messaging/Numbers/Contacts/Tags/Webhooks/Company/Integration/Analytics, etc.) with CRUD (e.g., Webhooks: list/retrieve/create/update/delete), indicating broad coverage. ([developers.aircall.io](https://developers.aircall.io/api-references))

verdicts.quote: “Aircall's MCP server publishes a catalog of tools… [Server URL:] https://mcp.aircall.io/mcp” ([aircall.zendesk.com](https://aircall.zendesk.com/hc/en-gb/articles/39677926959517-Using-Aircall-MCP-with-AI-assistants-beta))
verdicts.reason: Aircall operates an official MCP server (currently beta), so labeling MCP as “community” is incorrect.

verdicts.quote: “In order to access and use the Aircall APIs, You must obtain API Credentials for OAuth by registering for a Partner Account… In the event the Published Application uses Basic Auth, Aircall may require You to update … so that such Application uses OAuth.” ([aircall.pactsafe.io](https://aircall.pactsafe.io/versions/64bfbe34d99de9c22b12dd5a.pdf))
verdicts.reason: A generic, published connector would be expected to use OAuth (partner-gated) and Basic Auth for a published app can be forced to migrate, so Composio would need partner program approval to ship broadly. Additionally, API keys are self-serve to customer admins, but that path doesn’t avoid the partner gating for a multi-tenant/public integration. ([support.aircall.io](https://support.aircall.io/en-gb/articles/10375395181853))
